newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs may edge up, but much depends on data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs may edge up, but much depends on data.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) may rise a bit during Tokyo trade on Friday, partly in a corrective response to slides over the past few days, but direction is likely to depend to a large extent on economic data due for release in the afternoon, traders said.

The market is avidly awaiting Japan's industrial production figures, due out at 0430 GMT, with forecasts for July expected to exert the most influence on the market. May consumer price data is due at 0030 GMT but is not being as closely watched.
Moves of institutional investors will also be a focus after some investor buying was detected on Wednesday and Thursday.

A trader at a securities firm said there was some talk in the market that the July forecast for industrial production may not be that strong, minimising its impact and perhaps even prompting some buying. Other traders said the upcoming weekend may inhibit upward moves.

A speech to be given by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita at 0340 GMT will also be closely watched for any clues about interest rate moves. But a trust bank trader said that the chances seemed high that no fresh comments would be made, particularly as the speech will be just prior to the release of the industrial production data.
Traders said that some hedge selling may emerge ahead of the industrial production numbers, and any gains would likely to be met by pre-weekend book-squaring sales.

There has been market talk that some institutional investors may be a bit behind on buying, and that purchases could emerge after the industrial production figures, providing support. But afternoon and next week's moves remain difficult to predict and depend mainly on the numbers.
Economists polled this week by Reuters forecast increases ranging from 1.2 percent to 3.0 percent in May output, compared with a revised month-on-month drop of 0.5 percent in April.
